The seam was designed to host multiple platform-specific backends from the start.

lenny-qxx.2 (commit f80ba15, 2026-06-21) established the NativeBackend seam and AppiumBackend for iOS. The architecture was designed for extensibility: NativeBackend.press() already documents platform-specific keys ('iOS: enter/return/done/consent_accept/alert_dismiss; Android additively recognizes back').

lenny-qxx.5 (commit 331364a, 2026-07-10) proved the full Auth0 e2e round-trip on iOS with ASWebAuthenticationSession consent handling. All prior milestones (m1-m5) were iOS-only, leaving Android as forward-compatible scaffolding: NativeSnapshot.platform accepts 'android', native.press recognizes 'back', comments flag iOS-vs-Android divergences.

context.note: The spike design doc (docs/design/leonard-native-appium/backend_skeleton.dart) prototyped both iOS (XCUITest) and Android (UiAutomator2) patterns. It shows platform-branched capabilities (lines 146-163), Android selectors for Auth0 (lines 119-122), keyboard dismiss branching (lines 127-135), and notes the absence of consent alert on Android (lines 181-183).

AppiumBackend.enterText already branches on platform for readback: FN4 (line 481-487) reads 'attribute/value' for iOS but the comment notes it should read 'attribute/text' for Android. This divergence is scaffolded in comments but not implemented for Android backend.

AppiumBackend._dismissKeyboard (lines 512-533) branches on platform: Android posts to '/session/$_sid/back' (non-fatal), iOS 26 has no Done key (no-op), older iOS taps 'Done'. The Android pattern is ready to lift into a UiAutomator2Backend.

AppiumBackend._isSecureField (lines 496-507) detects SecureTextField only on iOS. Android UiAutomator2 does not have a direct parallel; the bead will need to handle secure field masking differently (likely by inspecting the element's input type or class).

The CLI (bin/leonard_native_host.dart:43-48) currently hardcodes AppiumBackend instantiation. It parses --platform but does not use it to select a backend. The bead must add branching logic: platform=='android' -> UiAutomator2Backend, else AppiumBackend.

The m2-spec through m5-spec documents (docs/design/leonard-native-appium/) anticipated Android handling at every milestone stage. The spec.md (lines 6-8) names FN4 as a hardening requirement: 'iOS reads attribute/value; Android reads attribute/text'. This confirms the dual-path attribute reading was part of the original architecture.

NativeSnapshot.platform field (native_snapshot.dart:100-104) is already wired: 'ios | android'. The snapshot is emitted by each backend and available to the extension and tools, so platform-aware logic can branch on it if needed (though the seam keeps platform quirks inside the impl per design).

The existing unit test (appium_backend_test.dart) covers iOS-specific behavior: masking flag derivation from element TYPE and the alert_dismiss endpoint. These tests will serve as a template for Android UiAutomator2Backend tests, though Android has no exact parallel to SecureTextField.

ADR-0006 (genesis/docs/adr/ADR-0006-pull-free-build.md, Status: Accepted) governs the NativeBackend design. The seam comment (native_backend.dart:2-3) explicitly references it: 'ALL device latency (WebDriver round-trips, a11y-tree polling) lives behind it; the extension never touches the device directly (ADR-0006)'. This remains the contract for UiAutomator2Backend.

The existing AppiumBackend uses http.Client injection for testing (appium_backend_test.dart:44-50), MockClient for unit tests. This pattern is proven and should be reused for UiAutomator2Backend unit tests.

NativeExtension (native_extension.dart:23-83) is platform-agnostic: it wraps any NativeBackend impl and exposes the same tools (tap, enter_text, press, swipe) regardless of backend or platform. No changes needed here; the backend swap is transparent to the extension.
The pub exports (leonard_native.dart:14) currently export AppiumBackend by name. When UiAutomator2Backend is added, it will need a similar export so the CLI (and tests) can instantiate it.

The native host e2e test (native_host_e2e_test.dart) already exists and drives the full Auth0 flow on iOS with the FakeNativeBackend. This test structure will provide the template for Android e2e validation, though a live emulator run is required (not just the fake backend) to prove Android.
